title: The rule of thirds — Image Wiki

rules.rule: If the subject is symmetrical and symmetry is the point, do not place it off centre as this destroys the intended effect.
rules.evidence: Symmetry. If the subject is symmetrical and the symmetry is the point, putting it off centre destroys the thing you were photographing.

rules.rule: If a horizon runs through the middle of the frame, do not use it because it splits the image into two competing rectangles with no clear winner.
rules.evidence: Do not cut the frame into equal halves. A horizon through the middle splits the image into two competing rectangles, neither of which wins.

rules.rule: If you are judging an image, do not score thirds-grid alignment as a quality signal because it is close to worthless.
rules.evidence: When you are judging images, grid compliance is close to worthless as a proxy.

rules.rule: If the subject faces or moves somewhere in the frame, ensure there is room on that side for the eye to go rather than placing it dead centre.
rules.evidence: A third, quieter benefit: off-centre placement leaves room on one side, and that room reads as direction.
